title: Accelerating protein design by scaling experimental characterization
abstract: Abstract Recent advances in de novo protein design have greatly outpaced standard protein biochemistry workflows, and experimental testing has been a bottleneck in the validation of new designs and methodologies. Here, we describe experimental and computational workflows to address the issues of scale, speed and reproducibility of common in vitro protein testing methods, enabling at least an order of magnitude increase in throughput while reducing wetlab time. Semi-Automated Protein Production (SAPP) is a rapid, modular, scalable and cost-effective protocol, enabling up to milligram-scale protein production, and standardized characterization including yield, dispersity, and oligomeric state of hundreds of designs per day, at the cost-equivalent of a few DNA oligos per construct. End-to-end protocol execution takes 48 hours, with about 6 hours spent benchside using mostly standard laboratory equipment. This protocol has become the standard at our institute, providing critical experimental validation for dozens of projects spanning tens of thousands of designs. We showcase the power of the platform by using it to rapidly characterize de novo designed inhibitors of respiratory syncytial virus. Since at least 80% of SAPP’s total cost comes from synthetic DNA, we also developed a scalable demultiplexing protocol (DMX) to leverage oligo pools as input DNA, providing a further 5-fold reduction in costs, enabling >1000 designs to be purified and characterized in arrayed, clonal format at a cost of $5 per construct. By reframing standard molecular biology practices and orchestrating wetlab workflows with partial automation instead of complex end-to-end robotics, these protocols should be widely adoptable, accelerating protein design.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the bottleneck of experimental testing in de novo protein design, which has advanced faster than standard biochemical workflows. The research sought to develop scalable and efficient methods for validating new protein designs.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study describes experimental and computational workflows designed to enhance the scale, speed, and reproducibility of in vitro protein testing. These protocols were implemented at the institute and tested on de novo designed inhibitors of respiratory syncytial virus.
analysis.methods: The methods involve a Semi-Automated Protein Production (SAPP) protocol, which enables rapid, modular, scalable, and cost-effective protein production and standardized characterization. A scalable demultiplexing protocol (DMX) was also developed to reduce costs by using oligo pools as input DNA.
analysis.main_results: The SAPP protocol allows for the production and characterization of hundreds of protein designs per day, with end-to-end execution taking 48 hours and most benchwork completed in 6 hours. The DMX protocol further reduces costs, enabling over 1000 designs to be purified and characterized at $5 per construct.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these protocols as a transformative approach that reframes standard molecular biology practices, enabling partial automation of wetlab workflows. This innovation provides critical experimental validation for numerous projects involving thousands of designs.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings have significant implications for accelerating protein design, which can inform the development of new therapeutic agents, including inhibitors for respiratory syncytial virus, thereby enhancing surveillance and treatment options.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is based on abstract-only information, and the study does not provide detailed results or limitations. However, the protocols are described as scalable and cost-effective, with a high confidence assessment due to their adoption as a standard at the institute.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the bottleneck in experimental testing of de novo protein designs by introducing scalable and efficient protocols. The Semi-Automated Protein Production (SAPP) protocol enables rapid, modular, and cost-effective protein production and characterization, while a demultiplexing protocol (DMX) further reduces costs. These methods have been adopted as a standard at the institute, providing critical validation for numerous projects. The findings suggest that these protocols can significantly enhance the speed and throughput of protein design, with potential implications for the development of new therapeutic agents targeting respiratory syncytial virus. The evidence is abstract-only, but the protocols are described as widely adoptable due to their reliance on standard laboratory equipment and partial automation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在解决从头蛋白质设计中的实验测试瓶颈,该设计的进展速度比标准生化工作流程更快。该研究试图开发可扩展且有效的方法来验证新的蛋白质设计。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究描述了旨在提高体外蛋白质测试的规模、速度和可重复性的实验和计算工作流程。这些方案在该研究所实施,并在从头设计的 呼吸道合胞病毒 抑制剂上进行了测试。
elements_zh.methods: 该方法涉及半自动化蛋白质生产(SAPP)方案,可实现快速、模块化、可扩展且成本效益高的蛋白质生产与标准化表征。此外,还开发了一种可扩展的解复用方案(DMX),通过使用寡核苷酸池作为输入DNA来降低成本。
elements_zh.main_results: SAPP 协议每天可以生产和表征数百种蛋白质设计,端到端执行需要 48 小时,大多数实验工作在 6 小时内完成。DMX 协议进一步降低了成本,能够以每个构造 5 美元的价格纯化和表征 1000 多种设计。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些协议解释为一种变革性方法,可以重新构建标准分子生物学实践,从而实现湿实验室工作流程的部分自动化。这项创新为涉及数千种设计的众多项目提供了关键的实验验证。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现对于加速蛋白质设计具有重要意义,可以为新治疗药物的开发提供信息,包括 呼吸道合胞病毒 抑制剂,从而增强 监测 和 治疗 的选择。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅基于抽象信息,并且该研究没有提供详细的结果或局限性。然而,这些协议被描述为可扩展且具有成本效益,并且由于被采纳为研究所的标准而具有高可信度评估。

abstract_zh: 摘要:新兴的从头蛋白质设计领域已远超标准蛋白质生物化学工作流程,而实验验证已成为新设计与方法学验证的瓶颈。本研究描述了一套实验与计算工作流程,以解决常规体外蛋白质检测方法在规模化、速度与可重复性方面的问题,使通量提升至少一个数量级,同时将湿实验室时间缩短。半自动化蛋白质生产(SAPP)是一种快速、模块化、可扩展且成本效益高的方案,可实现每日毫克级蛋白质生产,并对数百个设计进行标准化表征(包括产量、分散性与寡聚状态),每个结构体的成本仅相当于数条DNA寡核苷酸。端到端方案执行耗时48小时,其中约6小时为实验台操作时间,主要使用标准实验室设备。该方案已成为本研究所的标准流程,为数十个项目(涉及数万个设计)提供关键实验验证。我们通过该平台快速表征了针对呼吸道合胞病毒的从头设计抑制剂,展示了其能力。由于SAPP总成本的至少80%来自合成DNA,我们还开发了一种可扩展的解复用方案(DMX),利用寡核苷酸池作为输入DNA,进一步将成本降低5倍,使>1000个设计能以克隆阵列形式纯化并表征,每个结构体成本仅5美元。通过重塑标准分子生物学实践并以部分自动化协调湿实验室工作流程(而非复杂的全自动机器人系统),这些方案应具有广泛适用性,从而加速蛋白质设计。

title: Bovine Adenovirus 3-Based Viral Vectors for Veterinary Vaccine Development: Progress, Limitations, and Future Directions
abstract: Bovine adenovirus (BAdV)-based vectors, particularly those derived from bovine adenovirus 3 (BAdV-3), are emerging non-human adenoviral platforms for veterinary vaccine development. Adenoviral vectors are attractive for vaccination because they mediate efficient transgene expression, remain largely episomal, and induce robust innate and adaptive immune responses. However, widely used human adenoviral vectors, especially human adenovirus 5 (HAdV-5), may be compromised by pre-existing anti-vector immunity, supporting the development of rare human serotypes and non-human adenoviral alternatives. BAdV-3 is the best-characterized BAdV for recombinant vector engineering and has been used to express heterologous antigens from bovine herpesvirus-1, bovine respiratory syncytial virus, influenza virus, and Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Available evidence indicates that BAdV-based vectors can induce humoral, cellular, and mucosal immune responses and support intranasal antigen delivery. Protective efficacy has been demonstrated in selected experimental models, including mice and ferrets for influenza and tuberculosis vaccine candidates, whereas cattle challenge evidence remains more limited and is primarily represented by BHV-1 gD-expressing BAdV-3 vectors. These features make BAdV vectors relevant to bovine respiratory disease control, livestock vaccination, and One Health-oriented vaccine preparedness. Nevertheless, the platform remains at an early developmental stage. Key gaps include limited target-species efficacy data, pre-existing BAdV immunity in cattle, vector shedding, recombination risk, genetic stability, producer cell optimization, manufacturing scalability, and regulatory feasibility.

title: Molecular and clinical characterization of human adenovirus in hospitalized pediatric respiratory infections: a five-year study
abstract: Abstract Background Human adenovirus (HAdV) is a major pathogen of responsible for respiratory tract infections (RTIs) in children in China. This study analyzed clinical data from hospitalized pediatric HAdV infections over a five-year period to characterize the epidemiology, clinical manifestations, and associations with different genotypes and co-detections. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on 42,044 hospitalized children with RTIs admitted to Hebei Children’s Hospital between 2016 and 2020. Sputum were collected for viral nucleic acid detection and HAdV genotyping, along with demographic, clinical, and laboratory data. Statistical analyses included χ2 tests, Mann–Whitney U tests, and Kruskal–Wallis tests. Neighbor-joining method was used to construct the phylogenetic tree. Results Among 42,044 samples, 3,123 (7.43%) tested positive for HAdV. Of these, 1,954 (62.6%) had viral co-detection, most commonly with HRV, RSV, and HPIV. The highest HAdV infection rate occurred in children aged 1–3 years (χ2 = 418.44, P < 0.001). HAdV-3 and HAdV-7 were the predominant genotypes in both single and co-infections (χ2 = 22.227, P = 0.014). HAdV-7 was more frequently detected in patients with severe clinical manifestations, accompanied by decreased immune indices and elevated levels of procalcitonin, D-dimer, as well as cardiac and liver injury markers. Conclusion HAdV-3 and HAdV-7 are the predominant strains circulating in Hebei Province and primarily affect hospitalized children aged 1–3 years. HAdV-7 was associated with more severe diseases. HAdV genotyping sequence exhibit high genetic similarity across different countries.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在描述 流行病学、临床表现以及人腺病毒(HAdV)不同基因型及共感染与中国住院儿童呼吸道感染的关联。背景部分强调 HAdV 是儿童呼吸道感染(RTIs)的主要病原体。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对2016年至2020年河北省儿童医院收治的42044例呼吸道感染(RTI)住院儿童进行回顾性分析。该研究重点关注HAdV感染及其与其他病原体的共存情况。
elements_zh.methods: 收集临床数据和痰样本进行病毒核酸检测和HAdV基因分型。统计分析包括 χ2 检验、Mann-Whitney U 检验和 Kruskal-Wallis 检验,以评估关联性和差异。
elements_zh.main_results: 在 42,044 份样本中,3,123 份(7.43%)HAdV 检测结果为阳性。其中,1,954 份(62.6%)存在病毒共感染,最常见的共感染病毒为 HRV、RSV 和 HPIV。HAdV-7 在重症临床表现患者中检出率更高。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出结论:HAdV-3 和 HAdV-7 是河北省流行的主要毒株,主要影响 1–3 岁住院儿童。研究还指出 HAdV-7 与更严重的疾病相关。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果为 HAdV 在住院儿童呼吸道感染中的 流行病学 和临床影响提供了见解,可为该地区的监测和诊断策略提供参考。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于回顾性数据,这可能会引入偏差并限制建立因果关系的能力。由于该研究的观察性质和缺乏前瞻性对照,证据是中等的。

abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 人腺病毒(HAdV)是导致中国儿童呼吸道感染(RTIs)的主要病原体。本研究分析了五年内住院儿科 HAdV 感染的临床数据,以描述 流行病学、临床表现以及与不同基因型和联合检测的关联。方法对2016年至2020年河北省儿童医院收治的42044例呼吸道感染住院患儿进行回顾性分析,收集痰液进行病毒核酸检测和HAdV基因分型,并提供人口统计学、临床和实验室数据。统计分析包括 χ2 检验、Mann–Whitney U 检验和 Kruskal–Wallis 检验。采用邻接法构建系统发育树。结果 42,044 份样本中,3,123 份(7.43%)HAdV 检测呈阳性。其中,1,954 例 (62.6%) 进行了病毒联合检测,最常见的是 HRV、RSV 和 HPIV。HAdV感染率最高的是1~3岁儿童(χ2 = 418.44,P < 0.001)。HAdV-3 和 HAdV-7 是单一感染和合并感染中的主要基因型(χ2 = 22.227,P = 0.014)。HAdV-7 在临床表现严重的患者中更常见,伴有免疫指标下降、降钙素原、D-二聚体以及心脏和肝脏损伤标志物水平升高。结论 HAdV-3和HAdV-7是河北省流行的优势毒株,主要影响1~3岁住院儿童。HAdV-7 与更严重的疾病相关。HAdV 基因分型序列在不同国家表现出高度的遗传相似性。

title: Dissecting Immune-Epithelial Interactions in Airway Infection at Single-Cell Resolution Using a Compartmentalised Microfluidic Device
abstract: Immune-epithelial interactions govern the initiation and progression of airway diseases, yet their heterogeneity is difficult to capture using existing in vitro models. Although conventional Transwell and lung-on-chip systems reproduce airway compartmentalisation and permit epithelial-immune interactions, they lack the spatial and analytical resolution needed to visualise dynamic immune behaviour during infection. Here, we present the "Single Cell resolved Airway-Immune Recruitment" (scAIR) platform designed to interrogate immune-epithelial interactions during airway infection. The scAIR device features a modular central chamber accommodating a Transwell insert with primary airway epithelial cells (AECs) pre-differentiated under air-liquid interface (ALI), flanked by immune compartments connected through a precision-patterned microchannel array. This architecture enables real-time single-cell imaging of immune cell migration while preserving epithelial physiology. The scAIR device coupled with a machine learning analysis (MLA) pipeline enables automated tracking and quantification of individual immune cell speed, direction, and behavioural heterogeneity. Using this platform, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection is modelled to generate a type 1 inflammatory airway epithelium that drives neutrophil recruitment. TNF-alpha neutralisation with adalimumab reveals distinct migratory behaviours that are obscured by population-averaged measurements. This integrated platform quantifies airway immune responses during infection and therapeutic modulation, enabling mechanistic studies, drug evaluation, and precision modelling of airway inflammation.

title_zh: 使用区室化微流体装置以单细胞分辨率剖析气道感染中的免疫上皮相互作用

abstract_zh: 免疫-上皮相互作用控制气道疾病的发生和进展,但使用现有的体外模型很难捕捉它们的异质性。尽管传统的 Transwell 和肺芯片系统可以重现气道区室化并允许上皮-免疫相互作用,但它们缺乏可视化感染期间动态免疫行为所需的空间和分析分辨率。在这里,我们提出了“单细胞解析气道免疫招募”(scAIR)平台,旨在研究气道感染期间的免疫上皮相互作用。scAIR 装置具有一个模块化中央室,可容纳 Transwell 插入物,其中插入有在气液界面 (ALI) 下预分化的初级气道上皮细胞 (AEC),两侧是通过精密图案微通道阵列连接的免疫室。这种架构能够对免疫细胞迁移进行实时单细胞成像,同时保留上皮生理学。scAIR 设备与机器学习分析 (MLA) 管道相结合,可自动跟踪和量化个体免疫细胞的速度、方向和行为异质性。使用该平台,对 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 感染进行建模,以生成促进中性粒细胞募集的 1 型炎症气道上皮。阿达木单抗的 TNF-α 中和揭示了被群体平均测量所掩盖的独特的迁移行为。该集成平台可量化感染和治疗调节期间的气道 免疫应答,从而实现气道炎症的机制研究、药物评估和精确建模。

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究引入了 scAIR 平台,一种分区式微流控装置,用于在人类气道上皮细胞中模拟呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)感染。
analysis_zh.methods: scAIR 装置结合机器学习分析流程,可自动追踪并量化呼吸道合胞病毒感染期间免疫细胞的速度、方向及行为异质性。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: scAIR 平台提供了一种研究 RSV 感染期间免疫上皮相互作用的新方法,为了解 免疫应答 的机制和治疗调节提供了见解。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为开发更准确的模型提供信息,用于研究气道炎症和评估 RSV 感染的潜在疗法。

title: A novel combinatorial therapeutic strategy using resveratrol and viral oncolysis for diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma: an in vitro study
abstract: Abstract Pediatric central nervous system (CNS) tumors, specifically Diffuse Midline Gliomas (DMG) are a leading cause of cancer-related deaths in children presenting an unmet need for novel therapeutic development. In this study, we assessed the combined effects of resveratrol (RSV) and the oncolytic herpes simplex virus (oHSV), hrR3 in patient-derived diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma (DIPG) cell lines. RSV or hrR3 monotherapy resulted in a dose- and time-dependent reduction in cell viability. RSV pretreatment followed by hrR3 infection led to a significantly greater reduction in tumor cell viability than monotherapy. RSV pretreatment further enhanced the replication of hrR3, as evidenced by increased viral titers. Mechanistic analysis showed that the combination therapy was associated with reduced phosphorylation of the signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) and protein kinase B (AKT) signaling pathways, along with increased expression of apoptotic markers, including cleaved caspase-3 and Poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP). Together these findings indicate that RSV potentiates hrR3-mediated oncolysis in DIPG cells by enhancing viral replication, suppressing survival signaling and promoting apoptosis in DIPG cells in vitro.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to explore a novel therapeutic strategy for Diffuse Midline Gliomas (DMG), specifically Diffuse Intrinsic Pontine Glioma (DIPG), which are a leading cause of cancer-related deaths in children and present an unmet need for new treatments.

analysis.methods: The study evaluated the effects of RSV and hrR3 monotherapy and their combination on DIPG cell viability, with mechanistic analysis focusing on signaling pathways and apoptotic markers.
analysis.main_results: RSV pretreatment followed by hrR3 infection significantly reduced tumor cell viability compared to monotherapy, with increased viral titers and reduced phosphorylation of STAT3 and AKT signaling pathways observed.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that RSV enhances the efficacy of hrR3-mediated oncolysis in DIPG cells by promoting viral replication and inducing apoptosis.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide insights into potential therapeutic strategies for DIPG, highlighting the role of RSV in augmenting oncolytic virus effectiveness in vitro.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro findings, and the evidence is moderate as it does not include in vivo or clinical data.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated a novel combinatorial therapeutic strategy using resveratrol and an oncolytic herpes simplex virus (hrR3) for treating Diffuse Intrinsic Pontine Glioma (DIPG), a deadly pediatric brain tumor. The in vitro analysis showed that RSV pretreatment significantly enhanced the antitumor effects of hrR3, leading to greater cell viability reduction and increased viral replication. Mechanistic studies revealed that RSV modulated key signaling pathways and promoted apoptosis in DIPG cells. These findings suggest a potential role for RSV in improving oncolytic virus therapy for DIPG. However, the study's results are limited to laboratory settings and do not provide clinical evidence, which restricts the strength of the conclusions. The research contributes to understanding the mechanisms of oncolytic virus therapy and highlights the need for further studies in more relevant biological contexts.

abstract_zh: 摘要 小儿中枢神经系统 (CNS) 肿瘤,特别是弥漫性中线胶质瘤 (DMG) 是儿童癌症相关死亡的主要原因,对新疗法的开发提出了未满足的需求。在这项研究中,我们评估了白藜芦醇 (RSV) 和溶瘤单纯疱疹病毒 (oHSV) hrR3 在患者来源的弥漫性脑桥胶质瘤 (DIPG) 细胞系中的联合作用。RSV 或 hrR3 单一疗法导致细胞活力呈剂量和时间依赖性降低。RSV 预处理后进行 hrR3 感染,与单一疗法相比,肿瘤细胞活力显着降低。RSV 预处理进一步增强了 hrR3 的复制,病毒滴度增加证明了这一点。机制分析表明,联合治疗与信号转导子和转录激活子 3 (STAT3) 和蛋白激酶 B (AKT) 信号通路的磷酸化降低以及细胞凋亡标记物的表达增加相关,包括裂解 caspase-3 和聚 (ADP-核糖) 聚合酶 (PARP)。这些发现共同表明,RSV 在体外通过增强病毒复制、抑制生存信号传导和促进 DIPG 细胞凋亡来增强 DIPG 细胞中 hrR3 介导的溶瘤作用。

full_text: Abstract Objectives Invasive pulmonary aspergillosis (IPA) is a life-threatening opportunistic infection, most often seen in severely immunocompromised patients. In patients without classical host factors such as neutropenia, IPA has been described in critically ill patients with influenza and COVID-19. In past years, associations between IPA and other respiratory viruses have been made, especially in immunocompromised hosts. In our institute, we have recently observed multiple critically ill patients with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection and IPA, mostly in patients who had undergone allogeneic hematological stem cell transplantation (HSCT). We evaluated the prevalence and potential risk factors of IPA in critically ill patients with an RSV infection. Methods In a retrospective cohort study between January 1st 2016 and December 31st 2024 patients who had been admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) for respiratory support and underwent a bronchoalveolar lavage that was positive for RSV of whom clinical information was available, were included. Data regarding underlying disease, radiology, mycological tests, and mortality were analyzed. Results We identified 16 ICU patients that received respiratory support due to an RSV pneumonia. Of these, five patients (31%) had probable IPA, all of whom had undergone an allogeneic SCT. The 30-day mortality of IPA in these patients was 100%. Patients with an allogeneic HSCT and severe RSV had increased prevalence of IPA compared to RSV negative patients, albeit non-significantly (56% vs. 23%, p = 0.10). Conclusions IPA associated with RSV appears to occur limited to post-allogeneic HSCT recipients and carries a dismal prognosis. Acknowledgements Not applicable. Funding None. Ethics declarations Ethical approval This study was approved by the medical ethics review committee of the AmsterdamUMC, Amsterdam, The Netherlands in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the prevalence and potential risk factors of invasive pulmonary aspergillosis (IPA) in critically ill patients with an RSV infection, as IPA has been previously associated with other respiratory viruses in immunocompromised hosts.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted between January 1st 2016 and December 31st 2024, including patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) for respiratory support and who had a bronchoalveolar lavage positive for RSV with available clinical information.
analysis.methods: The study analyzed data on underlying disease, radiology, mycological tests, and mortality from patients who had undergone bronchoalveolar lavage for RSV infection and were admitted to the ICU for respiratory support.
analysis.main_results: Sixteen ICU patients received respiratory support due to RSV pneumonia, of whom five (31%) had probable IPA, and all five had undergone allogeneic stem cell transplantation. The 30-day mortality rate for IPA in these patients was 100%.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that IPA associated with RSV appears to occur primarily in post-allogeneic HSCT recipients and has a poor prognosis, highlighting a previously unreported association in this specific patient group.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that in immunocompromised patients with severe RSV infection, particularly those who have undergone allogeneic HSCT, IPA should be considered as a potential complication, informing targeted surveillance and diagnostic strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and potential for selection bias, with a non-significant comparison between RSV-positive and RSV-negative patients for IPA prevalence. The evidence is moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the association between severe RSV pneumonia and invasive pulmonary aspergillosis (IPA) in critically ill patients. It reports that among 16 ICU patients with RSV infection, 5 (31%) had probable IPA, all of whom had undergone allogeneic stem cell transplantation. The 30-day mortality rate for IPA in these patients was 100%. The authors suggest that IPA associated with RSV is limited to post-allogeneic HSCT recipients and has a poor prognosis. The study is a retrospective cohort analysis, which may introduce bias, and the comparison between RSV-positive and RSV-negative patients for IPA prevalence was non-significant. These findings highlight the need for targeted surveillance and diagnostic approaches in immunocompromised patients with severe RSV infection.

title: Opportunistic untargeted sequencing can complement targeted viral surveillance workflows for unresolved respiratory illness in Uganda
abstract: Routine respiratory surveillance in low- and middle-income countries relies heavily on targeted molecular diagnostics for influenza and SARS-CoV-2, leaving a substantial proportion of influenza-like illness (ILI) cases etiologically unresolved. To address this diagnostic blind spot, we evaluated the utility of opportunistic, untargeted shotgun next-generation sequencing of viral RNA on a small cluster of four unresolved clinical samples collected in Uganda in December 2025 that had tested negative via routine RT-qPCR. This opportunistic sequencing approach successfully identified clinically relevant viral pathogens in two of the four cases. From one sample, a near-complete genome of Human Metapneumovirus was recovered (13,273 bp, 45.6× coverage). This genome belonged to the globally circulating B2 lineage and revealed greater sequence divergence in the attachment G gene relative to the rest of the genome. The second sample yielded a 368 bp partial fragment of Human Respirovirus 1. These findings demonstrate that the opportunistic application of untargeted sequencing to diagnostically unresolved ILI cases can effectively complement targeted viral workflows, offering a robust, periodic tool to uncover missed pathogens in respiratory viral surveillance.

Page 2/14 Abstract Routine respiratory surveillance in low- and middle-income countries relies heavily on targeted molecular diagnostics for influenza and SARS-CoV-2, leaving a substantial proportion of influenza-like illness (ILI) cases etiologically unresolved. To address this diagnostic blind spot, we evaluated the utility of opportunistic, untargeted shotgun next-generation sequencing of viral RNA on a small cluster of four unresolved clinical samples collected in Uganda in December 2025 that had tested negative via routine RT-qPCR. This opportunistic sequencing approach successfully identified clinically relevant viral pathogens in two of the four cases. From one sample, a near-complete genome of Human Metapneumovirus was recovered (13,273 bp, 45.6× coverage). This genome belonged to the globally circulating B2 lineage and revealed greater sequence divergence in the attachment G gene relative to the rest of the genome. The second sample yielded a 368 bp partial fragment of Human Respirovirus 1. These findings demonstrate that the opportunistic application of untargeted sequencing to diagnostically unresolved ILI cases can effectively complement targeted viral workflows, offering a robust, periodic tool to uncover missed pathogens in respiratory viral surveillance. 1. Introduction Acute upper respiratory tract infections (URTIs) are the most common infectious disease cause for clinical presentations worldwide1 affecting productivity, driving unnecessary antibiotic prescriptions and causing a huge economic burden2. A substantial proportion of URTI cases go without identification of the etiological agent after routine diagnostic testing3–5.In many clinical and surveillance settings, diagnostic algorithms for Influenza-like illness (ILI) prioritize a narrow set of pathogens—most commonly influenza viruses and, more recently, SARS-CoV-26–8. While such targeted testing is efficient and cost-effective, it inherently limits pathogen detection and leaves a residual burden of unexplained respiratory disease. As a result, respiratory viruses with established clinical relevance may remain undetected, especially when case management or surveillance activities rely exclusively on targeted molecular assays. Untargeted metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) offers a complementary approach by enabling the detection of a broad spectrum of viral genomes directly from clinical samples without prior assumptions regarding pathogen identity9,10. Although not intended for routine diagnostics, periodic or opportunistic application of mNGS has been shown to uncover viral agents missed by conventional testing and to provide genomic data from infections that would otherwise remain uncharacterized11,12. In low- and middle-income countries, including those in sub-Saharan Africa, the diagnostic challenges are amplified by limited access to expanded diagnostic panels13. In Uganda, respiratory virus surveillance has largely been embedded within influenza sentinel systems, with broader respiratory pathogen testing performed mainly in research settings8,14. Such research has reported that a notable Page 3/14 fraction of ILI cases is attributable to non-influenza viruses, highlighting persistent diagnostic blind spots in routine respiratory surveillance3,15. However, untargeted genomic sequencing is rarely applied outside outbreak investigations or structured research studies. Here, we report the results of an opportunistic metagenomic analysis of nasopharyngeal samples collected from four (4) individuals presenting with flu-like symptoms who tested negative for influenza and SARS-CoV-2. This work was not designed as a systematic surveillance study but rather an exploratory application of untargeted sequencing, intended to demonstrate the value of periodically applying such approaches to unresolved respiratory infections on a cluster of individuals with flu-like illness who tested negative for influenza and SARS-CoV-2 (figure F1). 2. Results Four (4) participants were swabbed and tested for Influenza A and SARS-CoV-2 by real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). They presented with symptoms described in Table T1 below. All four were residents of Wakiso District in Uganda and adults aged between 31 and 53 years, with three (3) males and one (1) female. All four samples tested negative for influenza and SARS-CoV-2 by RT-qPCR, but two of them yielded respiratory viral sequence reads by shotgun metagenomic sequencing. Of these two samples, 1 revealed human metapneumovirus (hMPv) and 1 revealed human Respirovirus 1 (Table 1). Beyond these viral signals, all four samples yielded bacterial reads consistent with typical upper respiratory tract microbiota, predominantly Prevotella melaninogenica and Corynebacterium propinquum, alongside low- abundance environmental taxa common in metagenomic datasets (such as Phyllobacterium and Methylobacterium). No reads corresponding to those taxa were detected in the negative controls. Page 4/14 Table T1 Clinical characteristics and metagenomic findings of the participants 1 Age | Sex Clinical presentation Influenza / SARS-CoV2 RT-qPCR Shotgun mNGS (Relative abundance after host filtering | no. of reads) 36 | M Fever, headache, sore throat, cough, chest pain, rhinorrhea, dyspnea, vomiting, reduced appetite, weakness Negative Human Metapneumovirus (1.08% | 717) 2 53 | M Sore throat, cough, rhinorrhea, headache, chest pain, weakness Negative No significant respiratory viral signal 3 31 | F Fever, headache, sore throat, cough, chest pain, rhinorrhea, myalgia/arthralgia, weakness Negative Human Respirovirus 1 (2.7% | 18) 4 50 | M Fever, headache, sore throat, dry cough, chills, myalgia/arthralgia, reduced appetite, weakness Negative No significant respiratory viral signal Note: No chronic medical illness was reported by any participant. 2.1. The human Metapneumovirus (hMPv) case The hMPv case presented with the broadest range of reported symptoms and yielded the highest number of sequence reads on metagenomics sequencing. De novo assembly yielded a non-fragmented and unambiguous dominant contig corresponding to the near-complete hMPv genome (13,273 bp) with a coverage of 45.6× (supplementary figure S1). This has been deposited in the NCBI GenBank database under the accession number PZ228342. Phylogenetic analysis based on complete whole genome sequences placed the hMPv genome within the B2 lineage where it clustered with previously reported B2 strains from other geographic regions and showed no atypical divergence (figure F2). A BLASTn analysis of the sequence against the NCBI nucleotide database returned closely related hMPV B2 genomes, including sequences from China and the USA, with nucleotide identities exceeding 99%, query covers of 100% and e-values of zero (0). The G gene exhibited slightly lower sequence conservation relative to the full genome. When compared to both the RefSeq sequence (NC_039199.1), the nucleotide identity was 65.1% for the G gene vs 81.1% for the entire genome while comparison with its closest GenBank sequence, (PV218031.1), showed a nucleotide identity of 96.7% for the gene vs the 99.3% seen genome-wide. This reduced even further to 56.5% for the gene and 92.5% for entire genome, when comparing amino acid sequences. All coding regions of the recovered hMPv genome encoded full-length open reading frames without premature stop codons or frameshifts, and the predicted protein lengths were comparable to closely related B2 reference strains. Page 5/14 2.2. The Human respirovirus 1 / Human Parainfluenza Virus 1 (HPIV1) case The HPIV1 case, had a limited number of reads assigned to it. De novo assembly recovered a 368 bp contig representing approximately 2% of the genome, at low assembly coverage of 0.87×. BLASTn showed a 98.64% nucleotide identity to a GenBank HPIV1 sequence (MH828705.1) with 100% query cover and zero (0) e-value. To further assess the taxonomic assignment, reads mapping to the HPIV1 RefSeq genome (NC_003461.1) were examined individually, and their closest BLASTn matches consistently corresponded to HPIV1 sequences. The recovered 368 bp fragment mapped to the F gene of the virus and has been deposited in the NCBI GenBank database under the accession number PZ210030. However, the limited read count, low coverage and short fragment length prevented recovery of a complete genome and limited further genomic characterization. 3. Discussion Acute respiratory infections remain a leading cause of morbidity globally, but a substantial proportion of cases remain etiologically unresolved following routine diagnostic testing, especially since most diagnostic panels are restricted to a limited number of pathogens, commonly Influenza and SARS-CoV- 228–30. This diagnostic gap continues to be reported in both high and low resource settings, where so many ILI cases cannot be attributed to commonly tested viruses15,31,32. In this work, the opportunistic application of shotgun metagenomic sequencing to Influenza and SARS-CoV2 negative samples enabled the identification of other clinically relevant respiratory viruses, highlighting the importance of untargeted approaches in resolving unexplained respiratory infections. No respiratory virus was found in two (2) of the four (4) samples, but this does not necessarily indicate absence of infection. Rather, this may have reflected a non-viral respiratory pathogen or low viral loads for example during early or resolving stages of infection, which can fall below the detection threshold of shotgun metagenomics, a method which has a lower sensitivity compared to targeted molecular assays33,34. This limitation is inherent in untargeted sequencing approaches and should be noted when interpreting a negative result. Human metapneumovirus (hMPv) was found in one (1) of the four (4) samples and a near-complete genome of the virus was recovered. hMPv is a globally distributed respiratory pathogen first described in 2001 and is now recognized as a significant cause of upper and lower respiratory tract disease35,36. Despite its clinical relevance, it is not routinely included in many diagnostic workflows, especially in low and middle income countries during routine surveillance37. Moreover, to the best of our knowledge, this is only the second near-complete hMPV genome from Uganda available in a public database, following a sequence reported by our laboratory in 202415 (GenBank accession: PQ226465.1). The hMPv genome in Page 6/14 this work exhibited high coverage and was assembled as a single dominant contig which is evidence of a well-supported viral signal34. Phylogenetic analysis placed the hMPv sequence within the B2 lineage, a major lineage circulating globally. This is in line with previous reports of widespread circulation of genetically similar strains across diverse regions38,39. The integrity of the recovered genome was further supported by the observation that all coding regions retained intact open reading frames, and predicted protein lengths were comparable to reference sequences. The G gene exhibited reduced sequence conservation relative to the rest of the genome, a feature well documented for paramyxoviruses since their surface glycoproteins are highly variabile40,41. In contrast, the detection of human respirovirus 1 (HPIV1) was supported by a limited number of reads and a short genomic assembly. HPIV1 also known as human parainfluenza virus 1 is also a recognized cause of respiratory disease globally but is not part of routine molecular diagnostic panels in surveillance42,43. While the recovered fragment showed high nucleotide identity to reference HPIV1 sequences and similar taxonomic assignments at both contig and read levels, the limited coverage and short fragment length prevented comprehensive genomic characterization. This limited recovery likely stems from a low viral load or RNA degradation and highlights a limitation of untargeted sequencing in detecting low-titer infections34,44. Despite using a viral RNA extraction protocol, some bacterial taxa such as Prevotella melaninogenica and Corynebacterium propinquum, consistent with known upper respiratory tract microbiota45, were detected across the samples. The presence of these low-abundance taxa also reflects background signals common in metagenomic datasets, including potential contributions from laboratory environments46. This reinforces the importance of distinguishing clinically relevant pathogens from background microbial signals in untargeted sequencing. This work demonstrates that even limited and exploratory metagenomic analyses performed opportunistically can yield meaningful insights into respiratory virus diversity in routine clinical samples especially in regions where the full spectrum of circulating respiratory viruses remains incompletely characterized3,47. This work however, had some limitations including a small sample size and an opportunistic design that prevented inference as regards prevalence and epidemiological trends. In addition, the absence of virus-specific RT-PCR validation limited confirmation of low-abundance HPIV1 detection. 4. Conclusion This work attests that opportunistic application of shotgun metagenomic sequencing to diagnostically unresolved flu-like illness cases can reveal clinically relevant respiratory viruses that may not be detected by routine testing. The recovery and genomic characterization of a near-complete human metapneumovirus genome highlights the robustness of this approach, while the detection of a low- Page 7/14 abundance human respirovirus 1 signal speaks to both its sensitivity and its limitations in low-titer infections. These findings underscore the potential value of periodic untargeted sequencing as a complementary tool to targeted diagnostics, especially in settings where the full spectrum of circulating respiratory pathogens is not completely characterized. 5. Methods 5.1. Study Population and Sample Collection Nasopharyngeal swabs were collected from individuals presenting with flu-like symptoms in December 2025. Swabs were placed in Universal Transport Medium (UTM) and stored at − 80°C until processing. Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics of the enrolled participants were documented at the time of collection. 5.2. Nucleic Acid Extraction, RT-qPCR, Library Preparation and Sequencing Viral RNA extraction using QIAamp Mini Viral RNA Extraction Kit from Qiagen (Halde­ man, Germany) and RT-qPCR testing using CDC’s Influenza and SARS-CoV-2 Multiplex Assay were performed following the CDC protocol as previously described8. The RNA was then used to prepare DNA libraries for shotgun metagenomics sequencing with the NEBNext® UltraTM II Directional RNA Library Prep Kit for Illumina (New England Biolabs, Inc., USA) following the manufacturer’s protocol. The libraries were quantified and pooled for sequencing on the Illumina MiSeq platform using the v3 300-cycle kit, generating 2×150 bp paired-end reads. Negative controls were included during nucleic acid extraction and were processed alongside the clinical samples through the library preparation, sequencing and bioinformatic analysis. 5.3. Bioinformatics Analysis Raw sequencing reads were quality trimmed (Q30) using trim galore v0.6.1016 and the quality metrics were assessed using FastQC v0.12.117 and MultiQC v1.3318. Host-derived sequences were removed by aligning all reads to the human reference genome (hg38) using bowtie2 v2.5.419, and retaining only non- aligned reads. Taxonomic classification of filtered reads was performed using Kraken2 v2.1.320 against a standard reference database (https://benlangmead.github.io/aws-indexes/k2 accessed on 5 January 2026) to identify microbial taxa present in each sample. For viruses detected at notable read abundances (> 5 reads), pathogen confirmation was done using reference-based read mapping against their respective RefSeq reference genomes with bwa-mem2 v2.2.121. From the alignment files, the number of aligned reads plus depth were assessed with samtools v1.18 22 and the consensus genomes were called using sam2consensus v3 (https://github.com/vbsreenu/Sam2Consensus) - min. depth of 5. Page 8/14 In parallel, de novo assembly of non-human reads was performed using SPAdes v3.1523 and the resulting contigs were queried against the NCBI nucleotide database using blastn v2.14.124 to confirm taxonomic assignments and evaluate sequence similarity. Multiple Sequence Alignment was performed for the longest viral contig with other closely related GenBank and RefSeq sequences using Mafft v7.52625 (1000 iterations). Maximum likelihood phylogenetic tree construction was done using IQ-TREE v3.0.126 (1000 bootstraps) with the best fit substitution model chosen based on the Bayesian Information Criterion. The tree was then edited in itol v727 5.4. Ethical Considerations The data was collected and reported through the Health…
